items.title: Jimmy and Jeannie Cheatham interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 12, 1998
items.q: Count Basie’s music... they sort of leave him over here. And they’re always talking about somebody else over here. But he knew exactly how to maintain order.

ctx.x: We’ll have to sit and analyze that.

Well sure. But you know, Count Basie’s music, and for some reason a lot of the people that call them connoisseurs or want to write all about music, for some reason they sort of leave him over here. And they’re always talking about somebody else over here. But he knew exactly how to maintain order. He played his music and it corresponded to the heart beat. And he knew that. He was born to do that. He was one of the best at that, if you want to speak of something that he contributed. He really knew how to move and…

And the most beautiful thing, hearing a thirteen, fourteen, fifteen, now seventeen piece band — or five, etcetera — at the time it was smaller. When he’d say “bing” — look out. And the band would say — oh.
